title: A 1 minute backtest on free data cannot go back more than 60 days
author: person-person12
selftext:
A 1 minute backtest on free data cannot go back more than 60 days. yfinance is what nearly every free script and tutorial pulls from, and 60 days is its hard ceiling on 1 minute candles. So when a five year 1 minute result turns up on my feed, the candles underneath it were daily ones with intraday rules bolted on top.

**That swap changes which strategy you are actually testing.** On daily data your stop and your target usually both sit inside one candle, so the engine has to decide which one price reached first. It cannot know, and whatever it assumes there can be the difference between a profit factor above and below 1.0 with every rule left untouched.

**-----**

The reason the free libraries stop at 60 days is cost. **Intraday history is something somebody sells, so holding years of it across thousands of tickers is a bill that arrives every month.** The intraday equity history I test on in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) starts in 2000 and the futures roots go back to 2016, and keeping that current is the most boring expensive part of the whole thing.

Its a bit like learning to parallel park from a photo of the street taken at noon. You can measure the gap off that photo all day. You still learn nothing about the cyclist who comes past while youre reversing, because he was never in the frame. A daily candle is the noon photo of an intraday idea.

**-----**

Two things I check on any intraday result before I believe it, mine included:

1) the first and last candle the test actually used, not the date range that got typed in

2) whether the candles were smaller than the stop distance the test was told to respect

If the answer to the second one is no, the order of fills inside that candle was assumed. That assumption is usually worth more than the edge being claimed.
